newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines approves 20 peso hike in Manila wages.
newsitem.headline: Philippines approves 20 peso hike in Manila wages.

text.p: A government wage panel on Tuesday approved a 20 peso increase in the present minimum daily wage of 165 pesos for workers in the Philippine capital Manila, board chairman Michael Young said.

The wage adjustment will be effected in two tranches -- the first 15 pesos will be effective 15 days after the order is published in major newspapers and the next five pesos will be effective on May 1 this year, Young said.
Young told a news conference that the wage increase was only applicable to minimum wage earners.
He said the adjustment was made due to successive oil price increases over the past six months, higher transportation fares and eroding purchasing power of the peso.
Domestic oil prices have been rising in the past six months after the government partially deregulated the pricing mechanism.
"It's not a unanimous decision. It's merely a majority decision," Young said.
Employers' representatives have warned that the wage increase was counter-productive and could lead to inflation.
"Wage increases should be based on productivity," Vicente Leogardo, from the Employers Confederation of the Philippines (ECOP), said.
He warned that small and medium sized enterprises might close down due to high labour costs.
